im-c63-01.h: 기간 + 만에 (소요 시간과 경과) vs 기간 + 동안 (단순 지속)

a.d: Focuses simply on the entire duration throughout which an action persisted.
ex: 저는 대학교에서 4년 **동안** 한국어를 공부했어요. / I studied Korean for four years at university.

b.h: 기간 + 만에 (Elapsed time before resumption / realization)
b.d: Emphasizes the specific interval that passed before an event reoccurred or reached completion.
ex: 고등학교 졸업 후 십 년 **만에** 오랜 친구를 다시 만났어요. / After high school graduation, I met my longtime friend again after ten years.

im-c63-01.tip: 기간 + 만에 highlights reunion after long intervals (삼 년 만에 만났다) or completing something within a record time (두 시간 만에 다 끝냈다).

im-c63-01.why: Returning to visit hometown after an absence of five years requires 기간 + 만에.

items: I can recount long-awaited reunions and milestones using 기간 + 만에.

a.d: Extremely popular in daily spoken Korean to link causes to effects or consecutive steps in casual narratives.
ex: 어제 비가 많이 **와 가지고** 약속이 취소됐어요. / Yesterday it rained heavily, so the appointment got canceled.

b.d: The textbook and formal written standard for expressing reasons and temporal sequences.
ex: 어제 비가 많이 **와서** 약속이 취소되었습니다. / Yesterday it rained heavily, so the appointment was canceled.

im-c63-02.tip: In friendly spoken chats, Koreans frequently use -아/어 가지고 (어제 너무 바빠 가지고, 돈을 모아 가지고). In written essays, news, or exams, stick to -아/어서.

경제 위기가 심화되어 실업률이 크게 상승했습니다
im-c63-02.hint: Use the formal written cause connector -아/어서: 심화되어서 / 심화되어.
im-c63-02.why: In formal reports and news writing, use the standard connector -아/어서 instead of colloquial -아/어 가지고.

im-c63-03.h: -았/었다가 (완료 후 반전) vs -고서 (선행 동작 완료 후 순차 진행)

a.d: Action A is completely finished, and then directly reversed or followed by an unexpected opposite action.
ex: 백화점에 **갔다가** 사람이 너무 많아서 그냥 돌아왔어요. / I went to the department store, but came right back because there were too many people.

b.d: Emphasizes that action A was fully completed first, serving as the premise or trigger for action B.
ex: 손을 깨끗이 **씻고서** 식탁에 앉으세요. / Wash your hands cleanly first, and then sit at the dining table.

im-c63-03.tip: -았/었다가 involves a turnaround or reversal (갔다가 오다, 샀다가 환불하다). -고서 involves a sequential progression strictly following a completed first step.

im-c63-03.q: Fix the sentence where a completed sequential hygienic instruction mistakenly used a reversal connector.
im-c63-03.wrong: 외출에서 돌아오면 손을 씻었다가 음식을 드세요.
answers: 외출에서 돌아오면 손을 씻고서 음식을 드세요.
외출에서 돌아오면 손을 씻고서 음식을 드세요
외출에서 돌아오면 손을 씻고 나서 음식을 드세요.
외출에서 돌아오면 손을 씻고 나서 음식을 드세요
im-c63-03.hint: Use the sequential completion connector -고서: 씻고서.
im-c63-03.why: Completing the step of handwashing before eating is a forward sequence, demanding -고서 rather than reversible -았/었다가.

en: On a weekend afternoon I went to view downtown department stores, but turned the car right back because the parking lot was full.
Parking the car at a park near home, I bought a cool beverage and walked along the trail.
Strolling in quiet nature instead of bustling shopping malls, my heart felt far more relaxed.

im-c63-03.q: Why did the author turn their car around at the department store?

Crashing the car into a park tree
im-c63-03.why: -고서 marks that parking was concluded before the walk began.

b.d: Weaves 기간 + 만에, -아/어 가지고, and -고서 into an engaging real-world story.
ex: 삼 년 **만에** 만난 친구와 밥을 든든히 **먹고서** 이야기하느라 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요. / Reunited after three years, eating hearty food with my friend first, we lost track of time talking.

im-c63-04.tip: Mixing elapsed duration (만에), spoken causes (-아/어 가지고), and completed steps (-고서) elevates everyday storytelling.
